plan-for-the-10-release-from-its-install.text: Plan for the 1.0 release from its installed artifacts.
Issue 747, part of epic 731. This plan follows the specification. It orders the pull requests, names the decisions taken and the consumers to run before the first push.

lean-binding.text: Lean is the behavioural authority. This ticket changes no Lean statement, no on-chain script, no script hash and no wire format. Its model position is Below: release plumbing, evidence pages and the wording of an answer that already exists.

Preserved: the reader's classification order of the frozen model (network, release, active token, state) and its recognition of a state output, the registration, update, termination and batch fold statements, and the refusal of a write that the model refuses.

The guidance names a release; it adds no new refusal and no new acceptance. If a pull request finds that guidance needs a different classification, or that a script, hash or wire format must change, the work stops there and goes to the epic owner as a user story with the Lean clauses; nothing is invented.
Conformance and the model mappings are computed again at the release revision by the existing jobs; no row is added, removed or reclassified by this ticket, and uncovered rows stay uncovered.

rulings-in-force.text: Roles (2026-10-28, issue 767): folders and readers are application-neutral; the guidance reads the packaged release table and names no application in a neutral role.

The provider is the chain entry point (2026-10-20): every chain read goes through the session; users have a web page, Koios and a wallet. A journey that needs a local file from a registry's booker is a failure.
Release standard (2026-10-20): Linux packages and the Homebrew formula come from the distribution helpers and actions; nothing here adds a local packaging script.
Versioning: stay 0.x until this ticket cuts 1.0. Choosing 1.0.0 is the epic owner's.
The trie library's proofs are assumed sound.
Preprod: devnet is the default. A read of the public test network's protocol parameters for the receipt refresh, and any measurement on it, wait for the epic owner's go.

pull-requests-and-slices.text: Each slice finishes in well under two hours; the commit owner may cut a slice smaller, never merge two. Pull requests merge into main in order, each when its required checks are green at the head. Pull request 1 takes the audited process; pull request 2 takes one writer and one review before its push; pull requests 3 and 4 take one writer, with hosted CI as the gate.

consumers-to-run-before-the-first-push.text: Consumers to run before the first push.
a reader or command wording change reaches help snapshots, parser corpora (after rows), the documented flags check, the recovery partitions, the command reference and open datum's printed refusals;
a release table change reaches the packaged table's freshness test, the neutral and application inspect tests, the bundle assembly (the table travels in the bundle) and the verifier's route list;
a release workflow change reaches the release scope pattern, the declared checks that must be hosted, the workflow command resolution check and the job names the ruleset requires; no job is renamed;
a documentation control reaches the rendered documentation job under the runner's bare path (only Nix and Git on PATH), and every external command it calls is declared;
a new reference to shared mutable state in a test fixture needs its entry in the input and output census in the same commit.

seats.text: A ticket owner, a commit owner and a commit auditor, mute and persistent, in a read-only audit worktree. No other seats. The auditor writes its own gate table when it is seated; the ticket owner joins the two once and freezes the result before the commit owner starts. Every build and test runs in a named, memory-capped scope with a timeout; long gates run in the background.
